transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Avery Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CISO - Galaxy Fintech), Maya Li (Cloud Architect), Tomas Rivera (Compliance), Elena Gomez (SecOps)

Summary: Security review focused on encryption at rest and in transit, options for KMS and BYOK, HSM requirements and integration patterns, audit/logging expectations, and next steps to validate architecture for a pilot. Customer asked about key ownership, remote KMS latency, envelope encryption, and auditability. Redwood outlined supported patterns for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments plus HSM options and tradeoffs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Park: hey everyone thanks for joining today uh we'll run through encryption at rest in transit and key management options for redwood, i'm avery from redwood 

this is samira our solutions engineer um and i'll hand over to raj to confirm any specific goals he wants us to hit
[00:10] Raj Patel: yeah thanks avery, main things for us are ownership of keys, audit logs for all key operations, and a FIPS-backed HSM option if possible. also need to understand how latencies look if we call an external KMS during inference, that is critical for our 200ms p50 SLOs
[00:25] Samira Khan: great, that's exactly what we'll cover. quick note 





apologies if my audio stutters, new wifi. so high level: redwood supports three modes: hosted api (redwood-managed keys), dedicated (customer-owned VPC + option for BYOK), and private on-prem. for KMS we support AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSMs via external key manager integrations.
[00:48] Maya Li: when you say BYOK, do you mean we can import our keys into your control plane or do you hold wrapped keys? we have strict rules 


we don't want private keys leaving our HSM
[00:58] Samira Khan: good question. two options: 1) envelope encryption with a customer-managed KMS where redwood only stores data encrypted with a data encryption key (DEK) that is itself encrypted with a customer KMS key (KEK). in that flow, redwood never sees the plaintext KEK. 2) for dedicated/private we can integrate with a customer HSM via key-wrapping APIs or a KMIP bridge so keys remain in your HSM and only wrapped tokens or references are stored. basically we support BYOK where the root key material stays in your KMS/HSM; redwood holds wrapped DEKs.
[01:28] Raj Patel: and audit logs 

we need to see every unwrap/unwrap call? or at least key usage metadata so we can satisfy auditors.
[01:35] Samira Khan: you get both. customers using BYOK get KMS logs from their provider (aws cloudtrail, gcp cloud audit logs) and we emit application-level audit logs showing when we requested unwrap for DEK, which resource it was for, and the operator id. we can push those logs to your SIEM or S3, or you can pull from our logging endpoint depending on deployment.
[01:54] Tomas Rivera: what's the retention on those logs, and do you support immutable append-only logs for compliance?
[02:01] Avery Park: default retention is 90 days in the console but for enterprise we can configure longer retention or ship logs into your bucket with object lock enabled for immutability. we also provide signed audit artifacts on request for specific compliance events.
[02:14] Elena Gomez: can you explain the latency impact? if for every inference we call an external KMS to unwrap a DEK, that seems untenable for low-latency workloads
[02:23] Samira Khan: right, we do envelope encryption and cache DEKs in the serving runtime. typical pattern is: DEK is unwrapped on first use or rotation and cached in memory in a secure keystore in the runtime with TTL and rotation policy. unwrap calls are therefore infrequent. we also support local HSM proxies for dedicated/private that keep the unwrapped DEK in an HSM-backed process avoiding network round trips per request.
[02:46] Raj Patel: that caching approach sounds good but how do you handle memory exposure and key zeroization if a node is retired?
[02:54] Samira Khan: keys are stored in a sealed process and we perform immediate zeroization during graceful shutdown. for abrupt terminations we have a panic handler that attempts memory wipe; plus nodes run on encrypted disk and access is limited via mTLS and RBAC. we can share the implementation details in the security appendix.
[03:12] Maya Li: does redwood support CloudHSM or external HSMs for BYOK? or only cloud KMS?
[03:18] Samira Khan: we support cloud-managed HSMs like AWS CloudHSM and Google Cloud HSM, plus customer-managed FIPS HSMs via KMIP or PKCS#11 bridges. if you require HSM-backed key usage for every decrypt operation, we can do that in Dedicated or Private modes but note the latency and throughput implications 

HSM TPS can be a bottleneck.
[03:38] Tomas Rivera: TPS 
 
do you have guidance on throughput for HSM-proxied unwraps per second?
[03:43] Samira Khan: it varies by vendor. AWS CloudHSM typical 100-1000 ops/sec depending on instance. we recommend envelope encryption with local DEK cache for high throughput 

that reduces HSM ops to key rotation windows.
[03:58] Raj Patel: ok good. on key rotation 

what's automated? can we enforce our rotation schedule and have redwood perform re-encryption? we need rotation without downtime
[04:06] Samira Khan: yes, we support customer-driven rotation. with envelope encryption we rotate KEKs in the KMS, and redwood performs background re-wrapping of DEKs and lazy re-encryption of objects. for active model KV caches we re-wrap keys and roll nodes gracefully so no downtime. we can also run on a canary first.
[04:26] Avery Park: another note: for the hosted api if you choose redwood-managed keys that's simpler but you give up full key ownership; for enterprise you can choose BYOK and optionally HSM. which mode are you leaning to?
[04:39] Raj Patel: Dedicated with BYOK and HSM backed KEKs ideally. but cost is a factor 

want to see the price delta and any perf tradeoffs.
[04:48] Maya Li: also need network placement 

how do we ensure egress to our KMS doesn't traverse public internet?
[04:59] Samira Khan: you can configure private connectivity 

we support AWS VPC endpoints (interface endpoints), Direct Connect, and VPC peering. for GCP there are private service connections. all KMS calls are over private networks in dedicated/private deployments; hosted customers can use customer-managed endpoints for key operations as well.
[05:20] Elena Gomez: what's the model for access control 

who in redwood can request unwraps? we need separation of duties and least privilege
[05:27] Samira Khan: our control plane uses RBAC scoped to customer accounts; we map requests to operator IDs. for BYOK we require an explicit grant 

IAM roles or service account grants. within redwood only the serving runtime identity can request unwraps; human operator actions (support) are logged and require approval flows for access to key material artifacts.
[05:47] Tomas Rivera: do you provide PBAC or attribute-based access as well?
[05:51] Samira Khan: currently RBAC with fine-grained roles; we have ABAC-ish policies via tags in the roadmap. we can share interim policy recommendations.
[06:00] Raj Patel: any recommendations on key lifecycle policies 

rotation cadence, algorithm, key lengths? we've been using RSA 4096 for signing and AES-256-GCM for data keys
[06:09] Samira Khan: AES-256-GCM for DEKs is standard. KEKs in KMS typically use AES-GCM or RSA depending on provider. rotation cadence: every 90 days is common for high-security orgs; we support that. signing keys may be longer. we'll send a recommended policy doc.
[06:22] Avery Park: quick aside, do we need to consider data residency? Raj?
[06:26] Raj Patel: yes, customer data and keys must stay in EU for our EU customers; if you offer dedicated in eu-west1 that would satisfy but want guarantees for backup/replica placement
[06:35] Samira Khan: we support region pinning for Dedicated and Private and can configure backups to stay in region. for hosted we have region options and can enable data residency controls for enterprise accounts. we'll capture exact region requirements in the follow-up.
[06:50] Maya Li: regarding in-transit encryption 

TLS, mTLS between services? what's the standard?
[06:55] Samira Khan: all traffic is TLS 1.2+ and internal service-to-service uses mutual TLS. for private deployments customers can require custom certs and our agents can use your PKI.
[07:06] Elena Gomez: I'm thinking about disaster recovery 

how do we ensure keys are available? do you replicate wrapped keys only or full key material?
[07:17] Samira Khan: we replicate wrapped DEKs to target regions; KEKs remain managed by your KMS regionally unless you configure multi-region keys. if you want geo-DR we recommend multi-region KEKs or an active-active KMS strategy. we'll document failover steps.
[07:32] Raj Patel: are there any third-party attestations for HSM integration? we need FIPS 140-2 level 3 or equivalent
[07:38] Samira Khan: we can support FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs in the chain. cloud HSMs often have validated modules; for on-prem HSMs customers bring validated hardware and we integrate via approved bridges. our attestation doc will list supported HSM modules and versions.
[07:53] Avery Park: quick check 

any questions on encryption in transit vs at rest?
[07:57] Tomas Rivera: one more 

key compromise scenarios. if a KEK is compromised how quickly can we rewrap and what is the window of exposure?
[08:05] Samira Khan: with envelope encryption you rotate KEKs and re-wrap DEKs; exposure window is the time between compromise and rotation. we can trigger emergency rotation and prioritize re-wrap jobs; for large object sets we do lazy re-encryption plus a background full job. we'll help size the rewrap job to meet your RTO targets.
[08:26] Maya Li: what about secrets in logs or telemetry? sometimes traces include IDs or partial tokens
[08:31] Samira Khan: we scrub sensitive fields by default; logs contain references (key IDs) but not key material. PII is redacted and we can configure additional scrubbing rules for compliance.
[08:43] Raj Patel: for audit we need proof that redwood didn't access plaintext data. can you provide signed attestations for operations?
[08:50] Samira Khan: we can provide signed logs and a signed statement of operations for specific windows; for BYOK the definitive proof is that KEK material never left your HSM and that unwrap logs exist in your KMS. we'll work with your auditors on exact evidence needed.
[09:05] Elena Gomez: how about developer workflows 

when engineers need to rotate keys or test integrations, what's the recommended safe pattern?
[09:12] Samira Khan: we recommend staging tenants with test keys, using CI/CD pipelines with ephemeral credentials, and using Terraform + our provider for reproducible infra. we'll include example pipelines in the repo we send.
[09:25] Avery Park: switching to implementation notes: for Dedicated with BYOK we typically do 1) network peering, 2) IAM/service account grants for KMS access, 3) deploy a small HSM proxy if customer wants on-call HSM unwraps, 4) configure DEK caching TTLs. any objections?
[09:43] Maya Li: how is the HSM proxy authenticated to the HSM?
[09:47] Samira Khan: typical is mutual TLS and HSM client credentials or PKCS#11 tokens stored in a secure enclave. we can integrate with your HSM vendor recommended auth flow.
[09:58] Raj Patel: on the topic of support access 

what is the process? we can't have them with direct key access
[10:06] Samira Khan: support gets role-limited debug access and cannot retrieve key material; we can run F8 debug sessions where logs are redacted and we share only metadata. any escalation requiring key access is done with customer approval and under auditable processes.
[10:21] Tomas Rivera: can we get a demo or POC where you demonstrate BYOK unwrap, DEK caching, and audit logs end-to-end?
[10:27] Avery Park: absolutely 

we can provision a sandbox Dedicated for a 2-week POC. we'll include an HSM-backed scenario for your team to run workloads and measure latency.
[10:34] Raj Patel: timeline wise we want a pilot in April, production in June if the POC looks good. security sign-off is gating factor
[10:41] Samira Khan: noted. we'll aim to have POC infra guide and Terraform by next week.
[10:46] Avery Park: quick competitor check 

do you evaluate CloudGiant AI or ModelServe?
[10:50] Raj Patel: we did a quick eval of CloudGiant but they didn't have BYOK in the same way. ModelServe had an HSM offering but the performance was worse.
[10:58] Samira Khan: ok we'll include performance comparisons in the follow-up.
[11:03] [Long silence and side chatter as people jot notes 11:03\u201311:20]
[11:20] Maya Li: technical question 

for your runtime caching KEKs, is that per-node or shared across nodes?
[11:25] Samira Khan: per-runtime node in memory. we avoid sharing plaintext keys across network to reduce blast radius. there is a secure inter-node handshake for replication of encrypted state only.
[11:38] Elena Gomez: what about backup of DEKs 

are wrapped keys backed up to object storage? where are they stored?
[11:44] Samira Khan: wrapped DEKs are stored alongside encrypted objects in your tenant's bucket or DB; backups follow the same region/residency policies. since DEKs are wrapped, backups are safe as long as KEKs remain secure.
[11:58] Raj Patel: do you support customer-managed rotation hooks so we can orchestrate rotation across services?
[12:04] Samira Khan: yes we provide a REST hook and a terraform resource for rotation events so you can orchestrate via your pipelines.
[12:12] Tomas Rivera: compliance-wise, can we get a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert copy?
[12:17] Avery Park: yes we'll send the latest SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 cert in the follow-up package.
[12:22] Maya Li: regarding encryption at transit layer between model weights and runtime 

are model weights encrypted at rest in your caches?
[12:30] Samira Khan: yes model artifacts and weights are encrypted at rest; in Dedicated we can keep model storage in your VPC and optionally encrypt with your KMS keys.
[12:41] Raj Patel: small question on tokenization telemetry 

does redwood capture prompts or PII in telemetry?
[12:48] Samira Khan: by default we do not store raw prompts for hosted customers unless opted-in for analytics; customers on Dedicated or Private control telemetry. we can configure prompt redaction rules.
[12:57] Elena Gomez: one more, SLA and breach notification times?
[13:01] Avery Park: our standard enterprise SLA has 72-hour notification for security incidents and we offer faster escalation for premium plans. we follow a full incident response playbook and will share details.
[13:12] Raj Patel: ok great. can you summarize the actionable next steps?
[13:17] Avery Park: yes 

i'll summarize: 1) avery to send SOC2/ISO pack and security deck by 2026-03-27, 2) samira to provide BYOK runbook, terraform examples for aws/gcp, and HSM proxy design by 2026-04-01, 3) schedule HSM deep dive and POC provisioning for the week of 2026-04-06, 4) customer to provide list of region/residency requirements and compliance checklist items by 2026-03-30.
[13:45] Raj Patel: that works. thanks everyone.
[13:48] Avery Park: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and slack. end of call.

Notes on transcript quality: some words were mistranscribed (e.g., KV cache spoken as 'KV cash'), speaker overlaps noted at 11:03 area, small audio gaps from Samira between 00:48-01:00.
